subject: Fed Speak Turns Hawkish

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Shares surge:  CoreWeave ( CRWV )  boosts outlook , touts cash flow and targets 2028 profitability .

 Huang scandal: Is Nvidia's ( NVDA ) two-day pullback the "opportunity of an absolute lifetime?" 

 Strong demand:  Banks mull raising  Anthropic's ( ANT ) IPO price; here's the retail allocation .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Hot CPI 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
A hot CPI report has largely cemented the odds of the Federal Reserve hiking its benchmark interest rate next month. The data triggered the largest single-day surge in the two-year Treasury yield ( US2Y ) as bond traders priced in steeper rate hikes, while some Fed officials are taking on a more hawkish tone.

 Stubborn inflation:  The Consumer Price Index in October cooled from the prior month, but was still hotter than expected . Core CPI also topped estimates and was unchanged from September.  "It's another distressing report, borderline disturbing," Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee told PBS News Hour . He said the impact of tariffs on prices should've faded by now, yet it still continues. "Perhaps the most troubling part is that services inflation is not coming down, and is probably not mostly driven by oil prices or tariffs or things that might be transitory," Goolsbee noted. When asked about his colleague Christopher Waller being open to a half-point rate hike in December, Goolsbee said everything is always on the table. "We must get inflation back down to target, and it's going the wrong way at this point."   Fed faces a big inflation foe: K-shaped economy 

 More Fed talk: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson believes "further gradual tightening seems appropriate" for now as "inflation pressures are still very much with us." She said tariffs, energy and AI have all been pushing prices up. "Tariffs look like they're fading. Energy supply and AI demand pressures are harder to call. What matters for monetary policy is where inflation ends up once the effects of these shocks run their course," Paulson added. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan still backs at least two more 25-bp rate hikes, saying "it may be possible to move more rapidly this winter ." Fed Governor Michelle Bowman admitted that inflation has been more persistent than she anticipated. She expects tariff effects to wane, while energy price pressures should unwind when the Iran war ends. But "inflation pressures related to the AI buildout seem to persist ," Bowman  noted.

 Rate outlook: Analysts repriced their Fed rate expectations after the CPI report. Deutsche Bank now expects the Fed to hike rates in January, in addition to increases in December and March. It didn't rule out a 50-bp hike in December, but that's not its base case. "Hopes of a Middle East de-escalation are pulling energy costs lower," ING Economic and Financial Analysis stated, which will help give a subdued November inflation print. "But we won't get that until the day after the December FOMC meeting. The Fed may get a sneak peek, and that should give it the confidence to only raise rates by 25 bp." SA analyst Dustin Quasney pointed out that the market was betting on a December pause a week ago. "We got an election that put a political bill on the AI buildout, a solid job report, and a CPI that hit Waller’s exact number for hiking. Each one gave the Fed less room to wait."
